title: The non-vesicular cholesterol transporter GRAMD1C is a pan-coronavirus antiviral target
experiments_summary: 1. GRAMD1C knockout (KO) cell line generation: CRISPR/Cas9 was used to create stable GRAMD1C-KO PK-15, Vero-E6, Caco-2, and L929 cell lines; genomic edits confirmed by Sanger sequencing and western blot. Cytotoxicity assessed by EdU fluorescence and MTS assays. 2. Viral replication assays in KO cells: TGEV, PEDV, HCoV-229E, SARS-CoV-2, MHV-A59, and PDCoV were used to infect respective KO cell lines; replication assessed by western blot (N protein), RT-qPCR, TCID50 viral titer assays, and immunofluorescence assay (IFA) at various MOIs and time points. GRAMD1C overexpression in WT cells also tested for effect on TGEV replication. 3. Viral receptor expression analysis: RT-qPCR measured ANPEP, ACE2, and CEACAM1 mRNA in KO cells to determine receptor downregulation. 4. Bypass of viral entry using TGEV-BAC transfection: ANPEP-KO and ANPEP-GRAMD1C double-KO PK-15 cells were transfected with a TGEV bacterial artificial chromosome (BAC) plasmid; viral replication assessed by RT-qPCR. ANPEP complementation in GRAMD1C-KO cells was also performed, followed by live virus infection, RT-qPCR, multi-time point viral titer assays, and IFA. 5. Viral attachment and internalization assays: WT and GRAMD1C-KO cells incubated with TGEV at 4°C; attachment measured by RT-PCR after PBS wash; internalization measured after 37°C incubation and pronase treatment. 6. dsRNA and DMV analysis: Confocal microscopy at 3 hpi for dsRNA foci; transmission electron microscopy (TEM) at 12 hpi for DMV visualization in infected cells. Co-transfection of TGEV nsp3/nsp4 in WT vs. GRAMD1C-KO cells to assess DMV formation. 7. Colocalization and co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) studies: FLAG-tagged GRAMD1C co-expressed with HA-tagged nsp3 and nsp4 in HEK-293T cells; localization assessed by confocal microscopy with Pearson's correlation analysis; Co-IP to confirm physical interactions. Lipid-poor and cholesterol-loaded conditions tested. 8. Molecular docking and mutagenesis: HDOCK and HawkDOCK servers used for in silico protein-protein docking of porcine/human GRAMD1C with TGEV/SARS-CoV-2 nsp4; key residues mutated to alanine individually; TM-domain truncation mutant (ΔTM-GRAMD1C) generated and tested for interaction and colocalization via confocal microscopy and Co-IP. Functional complementation assay in GRAMD1C-KO PK-15 cells used viral replication readouts. 9. Cholesterol distribution and transport assays: CY5-cholesterol staining with ER marker (pDsRed2-ER) and dsRNA labeling for confocal imaging of cholesterol at replication sites. Filipin III staining for free cholesterol visualization before and after infection. Biochemical measurement of intracellular free cholesterol with a Free Cholesterol Content Assay Kit. Overexpression of full-length GRAMD1C, ΔGRAM, and GRAM-only domain constructs in GRAMD1C-KO cells followed by viral replication assays. Exogenous cholesterol supplementation in WT and GRAMD1C-KO cells under infection conditions assessed by IFA. Cholesterol-loading and lipid-poor conditions used to examine GRAMD1C-nsp3/4 colocalization dynamics. 10. Inhibitor (20α-HC) experiments in vitro: PK-15, Caco-2, and Vero-E6 cells treated with 20α-HC at various concentrations after infection; cytotoxicity assessed by MTS; viral titers and N protein expression measured; dsRNA confocal imaging performed; nsp3/4 colocalization measured with/without inhibitor; TEM performed in HEK-293T and PK-15 cells transfected with nsp3/nsp4 to quantify DMV numbers. Antiviral activity tested against HCoV-229E, SARS-CoV-2, PEDV, PDCoV, and MHV. 11. In vivo mouse experiments: Heterozygous GRAMD1C KO (GRAMD1C+/−) mice generated by CRISPR/Cas9 (exons 3–4 deletion); WT and GRAMD1C+/− mice (n=6 per group, ~8 weeks) challenged intraperitoneally with MHV-A59; body weight and survival monitored daily; liver pathology assessed by gross necropsy, H&E staining, and anti-dsRNA immunohistochemistry (IHC); liver viral titers by TCID50. For inhibitor in vivo studies, mice received intraperitoneal 20α-HC (20 mg/kg) at 24h and 12h before and after viral challenge; same endpoints measured.
